Yo yo yo! So we BLEW UP in people last night, super exciting! Now I'm a mod here, yayyyy. Some of you already put in some requests in the chat, or in my inbox. It sounds like the vulnerability is in that tokens generated by Amazon Web Services are easily predictable and not intended to be secure. These tokens were then used by apps to store personal data.

I finally found the original researcher's FAQ at https://www.sit.fraunhofer.de/appdatathreat/

I was wrong in my first reading. It appears that apps use a single token to authenticate every user, and assume that the token can't be retrieved from the code because it is compiled. IOW, same login information for every user of the app.
